steps: A service opens a local database transaction.
It inserts the corresponding outbox event with a stable identity.
Commit makes both durable; only afterward can a retrying relay publish the event.

lesson.scenario: A bike shop commits sale S-91 and its BikeSold event without a database-message dual write.
entities: stores event EVT-91 in the same transaction
awards points once per event ID

steps.title: Open one local transaction
steps.narration: The checkout begins a database transaction for bicycle B-17.
steps.outcome: No externally visible fact exists yet.
steps.invariant: Business state and publication intent share one atomic database commit.

steps.title: Commit sale and event intent
steps.narration: Sale S-91 and outbox row EVT-91 become durable in the same commit.
steps.outcome: A crash cannot leave a sold bike with no durable event intent.
steps.invariant: Every committed sale has exactly one stable outbox event identity.

steps.title: Publish after commit
steps.narration: The relay claims EVT-91 and sends BikeSold to the event stream.
steps.outcome: Publication is asynchronous and can be at least once.
steps.invariant: The relay never publishes an outbox row before its enclosing commit.

steps.title: Survive a lost acknowledgement
steps.narration: The relay retries EVT-91 because the broker acknowledgement was lost.
steps.outcome: The consumer awards 90 points once despite redelivery.
steps.invariant: Consumers deduplicate stable event IDs; the outbox does not promise exactly-once delivery.

steps.title: Mark publication complete
steps.narration: After acknowledgement, the relay marks EVT-91 published for retention cleanup.
steps.outcome: The pipeline converges without a distributed transaction with the broker.
steps.invariant: Published marking is retryable and never changes the committed sale.
